PLAINTIFE’S MOTION TO CONTINUE HEARING ON NCMEC’S
MOTION TO DISMISS PENDING RESOLUTION OF
PLAINTIFEF’S RULE 15(d) MOTION

Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine respectfully moves to continue the September 25, 2026
hearing on the Motion to Dismiss of Defendant National Center for Missing & Exploited Children
(“NCMEC”) until after the Court resolves Plaintiff’s Motion for Leave to File Supplemental
Complaint pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 15(d).

NCMEC filed its Motion to Dismiss on August 12, 2026 and has noticed that motion for
hearing on September 25, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. Plaintiff is separately moving under Rule 15(d) for
leave to supplement Count III with events occurring after the First Amended Complaint was filed

and is noticing that motion for hearing on September 25, 2026.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 29 Filed 08/20/26 Page 2 of 5 PagelD# 331

The Rule 15(d) motion bears directly on the pleading that will govern adjudication of Count
III. NCMEC’s pending Motion to Dismiss expressly seeks dismissal of Count III for failure to
plead intentional or reckless conduct and sufficiently outrageous conduct. Plaintiff’s proposed
supplemental pleading adds post-filing allegations directed to NCMEC’s subsequently
demonstrated knowledge, acknowledged distress, intent or recklessness, continuation of the
alleged course of conduct, and awareness of continuing injury.

Under Fed. R. Civ. P. 15(d), if supplementation is permitted, the Court may also order the
opposing party to plead to the supplemental pleading within a specified time. Resolving the Rule
15(d) motion first will therefore establish whether the supplemental allegations are properly before
the Court and permit the Court to determine what further response, if any, should precede oral
argument on NCMEC’s Motion to Dismiss.

Plaintiff does not seek an extension of the briefing schedule on NCMEC’s Motion to
Dismiss or withdrawal of that motion. Plaintiff requests only that oral argument on the Motion to
Dismiss be continued until the Court has resolved the Rule 15(d) motion and established the
resulting pleading and briefing posture.

Local Civil Rule 7(G) provides that a continuance of a hearing date requires Court action
and is not accomplished merely by agreement of the parties. E.D. Va. Loc. Civ. R. 7(G).

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff respectfully requests that the Court continue the September 25,
2026 hearing on NCMEC’s Motion to Dismiss pending resolution of Plaintiff’s Motion for Leave
to File Supplemental Complaint under Rule 15(d), while leaving the September 25, 2026 hearing
on Plaintiff’s Rule 15(d) motion undisturbed, and reset oral argument on NCMEC’s Motion to

Dismiss as appropriate thereafter.
